title: Arancini
description: Saffron risotto chilled until firm, shaped around mozzarella, peas, and ragù, then crumbed and fried. Sicily's street food. Makes about 16.
notes: The best arancini start as yesterday's risotto. Without ragù, a cube of ham with the mozzarella is the Palermo alternative.

steps.text: Soften the onion in half the butter, add the arborio rice, and toast for a minute.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time with the saffron, stirring, until the rice is just cooked and quite dry.
steps.tip: Drier than a risotto you would serve. Wet rice will not hold a shape.

steps.text: Beat in the remaining butter and the parmesan, spread thinly on a tray, and chill until firm.
With wet hands, flatten a golf ball of rice in your palm, add a cube of mozzarella, a few peas, and a spoonful of ragù, and close the rice around it into a ball.
steps.tip: Keep a bowl of water beside you. Rice sticks to dry hands and tears.

steps.text: Roll each in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry in batches in the hot oil until deep golden, turning so they colour evenly.
steps.tip: Too cool and they soak up oil and split. Use a thermometer.

steps.text: Drain and rest for a few minutes so the mozzarella sets slightly before serving.
